reference_use.conclusion: The snapshot (project d8d46c95, Mathlib 25730c7c) contains the frozen Ch06 Contract; Submission is byte-identical, so child types may use only contract, SimonGMT and Mathlib names. SimonGMT supplies currents, test forms, TestFormOnConverges, simpleNVector and the weighted approximate tangent plane with uniqueness at θ(x) ≠ 0. It has no tangential gradient for Lipschitz functions on rectifiable sets, no co-area formula beyond the linear case and no slicing; Mathlib has none of these either. Those results (Simon Ch. 2, 1.5, 4.10, 6.3–6.6; Ch. 3, 1.2–1.9, 2.1–2.10; Federer 2.10.25, 3.2.22) are therefore cited inside the child proofs. Mathlib does provide: McShane (`LipschitzOnWith.extend_real`), Rademacher (`LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt`), Lebesgue differentiation (`IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average`), `ae_ball_iff`, `measurable_fderiv`, Lusin–Souslin images, `alternatizeUncurryFinCLM`/`smulRightL`/`innerSL` and second countability of C(K, F). The interior product ξ⌞(G/|G|) is written with these CLMs and evaluates by `rfl` to ξ(ν♭∧α). All seven child types elaborate in the comparator scope with the intended binder structure. The parent type is kernel-checked from five of them (axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). None of the seven names occurs in the snapshot project or among the 260 DAG nodes. The chart-cover and C¹-chart tangent lemmas of the lipschitz-pushforward branch are not yet accepted, so they cannot be reused; no accepted declaration has an identical type to any child. These checks do not certify the analytic proofs.

subproblem.title: A countable family of test forms determines currents
subproblem.statement: For all P, k ∈ ℕ and every open U ⊆ ℝ^P there is a countable set E ⊆ D^k(U) (= TestFormOn U k) such that any two currents S, R ∈ D_k(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U k) with S(e) = R(e) for all e ∈ E are equal.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∃ E : Set (TestFormOn U k), E.Countable ∧ ∀ S R : GeometricCurrentOn U k, (∀ e ∈ E, S e = R e) → S = R
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. D^k(U) = TestFormOn U k: C^∞ forms ω : ℝ^P → Covector (Eucl P) k with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U. D_k(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U k: linear functionals S with S(ω_l) → 0 whenever TestFormOnConverges ω 0, i.e. there is a compact K ⊆ U containing all tsupport ω_l and, for every i ∈ ℕ, iteratedFDeriv ℝ i ω_l → 0 uniformly on K. This realizes Simon's 'countable dense set of ω ∈ Dⁿ(U)' in the proof of 4.5(2).
1. (Exhaustion.) Choose compacts K_j ⊆ U (j ≥ 1) such that every compact subset of U lies in some K_j (e.g. K_j := {x : |x| ≤ j, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) ≥ 1/j}, or closedBall 0 j if U = ℝ^P; any compact C ⊆ U has positive distance to ℝ^P ∖ U and is bounded).
2. (Separability.) Fix j and let D_j := {ω ∈ D^k(U) : tsupport ω ⊆ K_j}. For i ∈ ℕ let F_i be the finite-dimensional normed space of continuous i-multilinear maps (ℝ^P)^i → Covector (Eucl P) k and consider ι_j : D_j → X_j := Π_{i∈ℕ} C(K_j, F_i), ι_j(ω) := (x ↦ iteratedFDeriv ℝ i ω x)_{i} restricted to K_j (continuous since ω is C^∞). Each C(K_j, F_i) (compact-open = uniform topology, as K_j is compact) is second countable (`ContinuousMap.instSecondCountableTopology` from Mathlib.Topology.ContinuousMap.SecondCountableSpace: K_j is second countable and locally compact, F_i second countable), so the countable product X_j is second countable, hence so is the subspace ι_j(D_j); in particular it is separable and first countable. Choose a countable E_j ⊆ D_j with ι_j(E_j) dense in ι_j(D_j).
3. (Approximating sequences.) Let E := ⋃_j E_j (countable). Given ω ∈ D^k(U), tsupport ω is a compact subset of U, so tsupport ω ⊆ K_j for some j and ω ∈ D_j. By density and first countability there are e_l ∈ E_j with ι_j(e_l) → ι_j(ω), i.e. for every i, iteratedFDeriv ℝ i e_l → iteratedFDeriv ℝ i ω uniformly on K_j. Put ϖ_l := e_l − ω ∈ D^k(U). Then tsupport ϖ_l ⊆ tsupport e_l ∪ tsupport ω ⊆ K_j, tsupport 0 = ∅ ⊆ K_j, and iteratedFDeriv ℝ i ϖ_l = iteratedFDeriv ℝ i e_l − iteratedFDeriv ℝ i ω (`iteratedFDeriv_sub`, both C^∞) → 0 uniformly on K_j, while iteratedFDeriv ℝ i 0 = 0. Hence TestFormOnConverges ϖ 0 with K := K_j.
4. (Conclusion.) Let S, R ∈ D_k(U) agree on E. By the continuity field of GeometricCurrentOn, S(ϖ_l) → 0 and R(ϖ_l) → 0. By linearity, S(ω) − R(ω) = (S(e_l) − S(ϖ_l)) − (R(e_l) − R(ϖ_l)) = R(ϖ_l) − S(ϖ_l) → 0, so S(ω) = R(ω). As ω was arbitrary, S = R (`GeometricCurrentOn.ext`). ∎
proof_key_steps: Compact exhaustion K_j of the open set U.
Forms supported in K_j embed, via all iterated derivatives restricted to K_j, into a second countable countable product of C(K_j, F_i); pick a countable dense E_j.
Every test form is the D(U)-limit of a sequence from E = ⋃E_j (TestFormOnConverges of the differences).
Sequential continuity and linearity of currents: agreement on E forces equality.

audit.reason: The countable product of continuous derivative spaces provides countable dense families on fixed compact supports. Approximating differences satisfy the exact TestFormOnConverges definition. Linearity and the currents' built-in sequential continuity then prove equality.
